 By Joanna Guelas Updated November 19 2026 - 9:03am , first published 9:00am By Joanna Guelas Updated November 19 2026 - 9:03am , first published 9:00am Save Share Wanderers recruit Panashe Madanha (left) is trying not to overthink his first meeting with Adelaide. Photo: Con Chronis/AAP PHOTOS Western Sydney recruit Panashe Madanha won't let himself fall for one of the oldest tricks in the book when he faces former A-League Men club Adelaide United for the first time.

 BLACK FRIDAY OFFER - SAVE 50% All articles from our website & app The digital version of Today's Paper Crosswords, Sudoku and Trivia All other regional websites in your area Continue Wary of complacency against last-placed Adelaide and relying on his inside knowledge, Reds academy product Madanha is keeping it business as usual for a reunion on Friday night at CommBank Stadium.
 The Zimbabwe-born, Adelaide-raised defender is still close with his former teammates after four seasons at the Reds.
 Making his professional debut in 2022, the 22-year-old also rose through the academy ranks under senior coach and then-academy boss Airton Andrioli.
 Last year's wooden spooners, the sixth-placed Wanderers are itching to bounce back after suffering a 2-1 loss to a 10-man Melbourne City.
 Wanderers star Nicolas Milanovic had a late would-be equaliser ruled out for offside.
 Meanwhile, winless Adelaide - who are also playing intercontinental football in the ACL Two - are rediscovering their best after Joey Garuccio scored a 99th-minute equaliser in a heart-stopping 2-2 draw with Melbourne Victory.
 Both teams should be fresh and firing after a bye for last weekend's international break.
 Ask Madanha if he thinks his intimate knowledge of the Reds gives them an advantage and he'll reiterate Wanderers coach Ufuk Talay's message.
 "The boss always tells us that we always want to focus on ourselves and focus on what we do best," Madanha told AAP.
 "The same goes for this week."
 Still, Madanha won't lie about how strange it'll be lining up against his former club after switching colours for the first time as a professional.
 "I still got a lot of love for Adelaide. I still keep in contact with a lot of the boys," Madanha said.
 "I've obviously known Airton for a long time .. I've got an idea of the style of football he wants to play, and I know the players that I'll be up against.
 Jarrod Carluccio has made the most of his opportunity in the Western Sydney backline. (Steven Markham/AAP PHOTOS) "But to be honest, nothing really changes for me … when we step on the pitch, it's all business."
 Alex Gersbach is nearing full fitness after suffering a hamstring strain in the season-opening Sydney derby, while fellow hamstrung defender Anthony Pantazopoulos remains at least four weeks away.
 Jarrod Carluccio has impressed as Gersbach's replacement in a backline led by former Melbourne City championship-winning centre-back German Ferreyra.
 "We are a tight-knit group and German's an experienced player," right-back Madanha said.
 "I've been doing my best to continue to build a connection with him (Ferreyra), learning off of him, and taking it game by game, building that partnership.
 "That's one thing we take pride in."
